service.description: Authorize (authOnlyTransaction) with the single-use browser token (paymentToken: Accept.js opaqueData dataDescriptor and dataValue), else with the payment method's customer payment profile (gatewayCustomerId and gatewayCimId at this gateway). A payment with neither is refused (NO_PAYMENT_PROFILE): card numbers are not sent from the server. The idempotency key's first 20 characters go in refId and order.invoiceNumber, which a lookup searches after a lost answer; a held transaction (fraud review) is pending with its reference.
A sale (authCaptureTransaction): as authorize#Payment, captured at once. Configure it as the authorizeServiceName with no captureServiceName.

Accept Hosted (authOnlyTransaction on Authorize.Net's page): nothing is sent; the payment waits at the hosted page (a response with transactionStatus HostedPending and no result), which the frontend's relay opens with a fresh form token (get#HostedPaymentForm), and the details lookup finds the payer's transaction by the attempt's reference (the idempotency key's first 20 characters, in refId and order.invoiceNumber). Needs the https returnUrl Mantle builds.
Accept Hosted as a sale (authCaptureTransaction): as authorizeHosted#Payment, captured on the page. Configure it with no captureServiceName.

A fresh Accept Hosted form token for a payment waiting at its hosted page (getHostedPaymentPageRequest), asked on each call and never stored: its amount and transaction type, the attempt's reference, the canonical return and cancel addresses (https, Mantle's), the receipt shown and the merchant's name. Answers the page's address (accept.authorize.net, or test.authorize.net for a sandbox connection) and the token, which the caller posts at once; the token's time is kept on the pending answer, after which (15 minutes and the lookup grace) a payment found nowhere is cancelled.

After an approved Accept Hosted payment its payer asked to keep (F40): the transaction's customer payment profile, else one made from it (createCustomerProfileFromTransactionRequest, onto the party's customer profile when it has one), kept on a new payment method (references and masked card only) that the payment then names.
Capture an authorization (priorAuthCaptureTransaction), the whole or a smaller amount. A capture the provider says was already done (reason 311) is a success.
Void an authorization (voidTransaction). A void the provider says was already done (reason 310) is a success.

Refund linked to the captured transaction (refundTransaction with refTransId; never an unlinked credit). The transaction's settlement decides, read first: settled, a refund of the amount (to its customer payment profile, else to the card's last four digits); captured and not settled, a void of the whole amount recorded as the refund (reasonCode VOID_BEFORE_SETTLEMENT); a partial refund before settlement is refused (REFUND_BEFORE_SETTLEMENT) and nothing is sent.

The payment's transaction status (getTransactionDetails by its reference), as a Payment status. For a lost operation (idempotencyKey given) answers operationFound: a capture or void on the authorization's transaction status; an authorization, sale or refund by its reference (transrefId, then the invoice numbers of the unsettled transactions held for review (pendingApproval) and of the others, then those of the batches settled since). A PgoTxDetails response records a change only. None found answers false once the lost request is older than lookupGraceSeconds (and the duplicate window); a search that could not be done leaves it unknown.

Make a reusable customer payment profile from a single-use browser token, on the party's customer profile at the gateway (made when none of its payment methods there has one). The payment method (the given one, else a new credit card method) keeps gatewayCustomerId, gatewayCimId and the gateway, and only the masked card; the token is not kept. Refuses a method of another party and a call without a token.

parameter.name: partyId
parameter.description: The owner; defaults to the method's

service.description: Delete the payment method's payment profile at its Authorize.Net gateway and clear gatewayCimId. A failure is a warning and keeps the reference, to delete again; the customer profile is kept for the party's other methods.

The receive service of AuthorizeNetWebhook. The endpoint /rest/sm/AuthorizeNetWebhook/{remote} checked X-ANET-Signature (the remote's SmatHmacSha512 and sharedSecret, the signature key) over this body; this keeps the notification once per remote and notificationId (store#ReceivedSystemMessage), so a repeated delivery answers success and is not consumed again.

parameter.name: duplicateOfId
parameter.description: The message already kept for this notification

service.description: The consume service of AuthorizeNetWebhook: a transaction event leads to get#SinglePaymentGatewayDetails of the payment it is about, among the payments of the gateways on the message's remote (by transaction id, else the refId of a lost operation). The provider's status is read by the lookup, not taken from the payload, so repeated, late and out-of-order events converge.

The public values a browser needs to tokenize a card for this payment with Accept.js: the API login id, the public client key and the script addresses of the connection's environment, and the amount to show. Only the payer, or a user with treasury authority over the organization paid; only an open (promised or declined) payment of an Authorize.Net gateway.

Authorize the payment with the browser's single-use Accept.js opaque data; with savePaymentMethod (the payer's consent to keep the card; ignored for anyone but the payer), first make a customer payment profile from it, put that method on the payment and authorize with the profile, and delete it again when the card is declined. The payment is locked and checked again; a replay, or an earlier authorization still pending or unknown, sends nothing and makes no profile (state pending or unknown). A payment method of another gateway is refused. The payment decides the organization, gateway, amount and currency; the browser gives only the token, the consent and an operation id (a retry with the same id is answered from the first response). The answer is the gateway response's state: approved, declined, pending, unknown or error. Access as get#BrowserPaymentConfig.

parameter.name: operationId
parameter.description: 8 to 40 letters, digits, - or _, made once per page
